en: In the Supreme Self, there is non-duality between Śrīnātha and Jānakīnātha;
nevertheless, for me, the lotus-eyed Rāma is my everything.
Oṃ, salutations to Śrī Rāmacandra.
This hymn [is composed] of phonemes, clusters of meanings, aesthetic sentiments, and also meters.
I pay homage to Vāṇī and Vināyaka, the two makers of auspiciousness. || 1 ||
I bow to Bhavānī and Śaṅkara, who are the embodiments of faith and trust;
without whom even the perfected ones do not perceive the Lord dwelling within their own hearts.
I eternally salute the Guru in the form of Śaṅkara, who consists of pure awakening;
for even the moon, though crooked, is honored everywhere because it relies upon him. || 3 ||
I salute the two lords of poets and monkeys, whose pure consciousnesses dwell in the holy forest of the multitude of virtues of Sītā and Rāma. 4.
I bow to Sītā, the beloved of Rāma, who brings about creation, preservation, and dissolution; who removes afflictions; who bestows all auspiciousness; and who is the source of all welfare. || 5 ||
The entire universe, including all the gods and asuras headed by Brahmā, is subject to His māyā;
because of its existence, everything appears as if it were real, just as the delusion of a snake appears in a rope.
Indeed, for those desiring to cross the ocean of worldly existence, it is only the boat of His feet that truly shines forth.
I bow to that Lord Hari, known as Rāma, who is the supreme cause of all without exception.

May that beauty of the lotus-face of my joy of the Raghus, which did not lose its clarity despite the consecration and did not wither from the hardships of dwelling in the forest, always grant me auspicious and lovely blessings. 7.
I bow to Rāma, the lord of the Raghu dynasty, whose delicate limbs are dark like a blue lotus, whose left side is occupied by Sītā, and who holds in his hand a beautiful bow with a great arrow.
The root of the tree of Dharma, the full moon from the ocean of solitude that bestows bliss,
the sun for the lotus of dispassion, the remover of sin, the dispeller of darkness and suffering,
the sky-born Śaṅkara who performs the task of rending the mass of clouds of delusion— [I bow to him].
I pay homage to the beloved of King Śrī Rāma, who dwells in the family of Brahmā and quiets all blemishes. || 9 ||
I bow to that most excellent one, whose body possesses the auspiciousness of dense clouds of bliss, who is clad in yellow garments and is beautiful;
who holds a bow and arrows in his hand, bears the weight of quivers at his waist,
has large lotus-like eyes, and is graced by a mass of matted locks.
I worship Rāma, who is delightful, accompanied by Sītā and Lakṣmaṇa, and traveling upon the path. || 10 ||
The two foremost of the Raghus, who possess supreme power as beautiful as a jasmine flower and a blue lotus, who are the abodes of consciousness,
rich in splendor, wielders of excellent bows, praised by the Vedas, beloved by the multitudes of cows and brahmins,
who assume illusory human forms, are endowed with true dharma and are beneficent.
For those two, intent on searching for Sītā, have come upon our path and have bestowed their devotion upon us. || 11 ||
Born from the ocean of Brahmā, the destroyer of the impurities of the Kali age, imperishable, and eternally graced by the beautiful moon-like face of the illustrious Śambhu;
the medicine for the disease of saṃsāra, the bestower of happiness, the very life of the illustrious Jānakī.
Blessed are those fortunate ones who constantly drink the nectar of the name of Śrī Rāma.

I bow to Hari, known as Rāma, the Lord of the universe and preceptor of the gods; who is peaceful, eternal, immeasurable, and sinless; who bestows the peace of Nirvāṇa; who is served incessantly by Brahmā, Śambhu, and the king of serpents; who is the all-pervading one to be known through the Vedāntas; and who, though appearing as a human through Māyā, is the Supreme Lord.
I bow to the mine of compassion, the best of the Raghus, the crest-jewel of kings.
Dark blue like the throat of a peacock, marked with the lotus-feet of the radiant gods, rich in splendor, clad in yellow garments, lotus-eyed, ever-pleased,
holding a reed-arrow and a bow in his hand, accompanied by a host of monkeys, and served by his kinsman— [I meditate upon Him].
I perpetually bow to the worshipful Lord of Janaki, the best of the Raghus, Rāma, who is mounted upon the Puṣpaka chariot.
I bow to that Rāmacandra, the destroyer of the suffering of the afflicted, the dispeller of the fear of the frightened, and the rod of Time for his enemies. 15.
To Śrī Rāghava, the son of Daśaratha, the immeasurable Lord of Sītā, the jewel-lamp of the lineage of Raghu’s clan,
whose arms reach to his knees and whose eyes are as broad as lotus petals—
I bow to Rāma, the destroyer of night-stalkers. || 16 ||
Accompanied by Vaidehī, he was seated upon a jeweled *vīrāsana* throne in the midst of a great golden pavilion beneath a celestial tree in the Puṣpaka chariot;
before him, the son of the Wind-god recited the supreme reality as expounded by the lords of sages.
I worship the dark-complexioned Rāma, surrounded by Bharata and the others, as described [in the scriptures]. || 17 ||
O Lord of the Raghus, I tell you truly: there is no other longing or desire in my heart; for you are the inner self of all beings.
O best of the Raghus, grant me intense devotion and make my mind free from defects such as desire and the like.
Oṃ, salutations to the Supreme Brahman, the illustrious Rāmacandra, accompanied by Śrī Sītā, Lakṣmaṇa, Bharata, Śatrughna, and Hanumān.
Now begins the proclamation:
Bālakāṇḍa 1. O Rāma, supreme beyond the Supreme, pure Brahman!
O Supreme Lord Rāma, whose very nature is Time.
O Rāma, who sleeps happily upon the couch of Śeṣa;
O Rāma, entreated by Brahmā and the other immortals.
5. O Rāma, ornament of the solar dynasty!
6. O Rāma, joy of the illustrious Daśaratha!
7. O Rāma, who increases the happiness of Kauśalyā! 8. O Rāma, who is the beloved treasure of Viśvāmitra!
9. O Rāma, slayer of the terrible Tāṭakā! 10. O Rāma, destroyer of Mārīca and the others!
11. O Rāma, protector of Kauśika’s sacrifice!
12. O Śrīmad-Ahalyoddhāraka Rāma!
O Rāma, worshipped by the sage Gautama! O Rāma, praised by the hosts of gods and the best of sages!
15. O Rāma, whose gentle footsteps cause the boatmen to run!
16. O Rāma, who enchants the people of the city of Mithilā!
17. O Rāma, who delights the mind of the bodiless one (Kāmadeva).
18. O Rāma, who broke the bow of Tryambaka (Śiva).
19. O Rāma, who bestowed the excellent garland upon Sītā!
20. O Rāma, who performed the auspicious wedding rites!
O Rāma, destroyer of the pride of Bhārgava;
O Rāma, protector of glorious Ayodhyā.
Rāma,
adorned with an immeasurable multitude of virtues; Rāma,
desired by the daughter of the earth.
25. O Rāma, whose face is like the full moon!
26. O Rāma, who has taken refuge in the forest at the word of his father!
O Rāma, whose feet were pointed out by Priyaguha;
O Rāma, whose own soft feet were washed by him.
O Rāma, who brings joy to the face of Bharadvāja!
O Rāma, whose dwelling is on Mount Citrakūṭa!
O Rāma, long contemplated by Daśaratha;
O Rāma, requested by Kaikeyī’s son.
O Rāma, who performed the funeral rites for your own father; O Rāma, who entrusted your own sandals to Bharata.
O Rāma,
purifier of the Daṇḍaka forest region! O Rāma,
destroyer of the wicked Virādha!
O Rāma, honored by Śarabhaṅga and Sutīkṣṇa! O Rāma, increased by the grace of Agastya!
O Rāma, served by the lord of vultures!
O Rāma, well-established on the banks of Pañcavaṭī!
O Rāma, who caused the suffering of Śūrpaṇakhā!
O Rāma, who slew Khara, Dūṣaṇa, and the others!
43. O Rāma, followed by the deer dear to Sītā!
44. O Rāma, who sent the arrow that caused distress to Mārīca!
O Rāma, seeker of the lost Sītā!
O Rāma, bestower of the state of the king of vultures!
O Rāma, who ate the fruit offered by Śabarī! O Rāma, who severed the arms of Kabandha!
Rāma, whose own station was served by Hanumān in the Kiṣkindhā-kāṇḍa;
Rāma, who grants the desires of the prostrate Sugrīva.
51. O Rāma, destroyer of the arrogant Bāli;
52. O Rāma, sender of the monkey-messenger.
53. O Rāma, accompanied by Lakṣmaṇa, who acts for the benefit [of all];
54. O Rāma, constantly remembered by the foremost of monkeys; Sundarakāṇḍa.
O Rāma, destroyer of obstacles to her progress! O Rāma, sustainer of Sītā’s life!
O Rāma, who was defiled by the wicked Daśānana; O Rāma, who was adorned by the virtuous Hanumān.
59. Rāma, who was informed by Sītā regarding the Kākā forest.
60. Rāma, who beheld the crest-jewel (of Rāvaṇa).
61 || Rāma, comforted by the words of the foremost of monkeys;
the Yuddhakāṇḍa,
62 || Rāma, set forth for the destruction of Rāvaṇa.
O Rāma, surrounded by the monkey army!
O Rāma, who dried up the ocean at the request of the Lord of Rivers!
65. O Rāma, bestower of fearlessness upon Vibhīṣaṇa!
66. O Rāma, builder of the bridge across the mountain range!
O Rāma, the one who severed the head of Kumbhakarṇa! O Rāma, the one who crushed the hosts of rākṣasas!
O Rāma, who subdued Ahi, Ahirāvaṇa, and Cāraṇa!
O Rāma, who destroyed the ten-faced Rāvaṇa!
O Rāma, praised by the gods headed by Brahmā;
O Rāma, beheld by Daśaratha stationed in the sky.
73. O Rāma, delighted by the sight of Sītā; 74. O Rāma, bowed to by Vibhīṣaṇa after his consecration.
75. Rama’s ascent onto the Puṣpaka chariot;
76. Rama’s visit to Bharadvāja.
O Rāma, who makes Bharata dearer than life! O Rāma, the ornament of the city of Sāketa!
79. O Rāma, who regards all as equal to yourself!
80. O Rāma, seated upon a throne resplendent with jewels!
81) O Rāma, adorned by the ceremony of coronation;
82) O Rāma, honored by the lineage of kings.
O Rāma, who granted the kingdom to Vibhīṣaṇa;
O Rāma, who bestowed grace upon the host of monkeys!
85. O Rāma, protector of all living beings! 86. O Rāma, support of all the worlds!
O Rāma, praised by the hosts of sages who have arrived!
(87) O Rāma, born from the renowned Ten-necked one! (88)
89. O Rāma, blissful from embracing Sītā!
90. O Rāma, whose kingdom is well-protected by statesmanship!
O Rāma, who caused the daughter of Janaka to abandon the forest;
O Rāma, who brought about the slaying of the demon Lavaṇa.
O Rāma, praised by Śambuka who has gone to heaven; O Rāma, delighted by the welfare of your own sons Kuśa and Lava.
95. O Rāma, initiated for the horse-sacrifice!
96. O Rāma, who has made known the state of the gods through time!
O Rāma, the bestower of liberation upon the people of Ayodhyā!
O Rāma, the delighter of the gods from the mouth of Brahmā!
O Rāma, whose own form is composed of light!
O Rāma, who releases one from the bonds of worldly existence!
101 || O Rāma, intent upon the establishment of Dharma! 102 || O Rāma, devoted to devotion and the giver of liberation!
103. O Rāma, protector of all that is moving and unmoving! 104. O Rāma, warder-off of the disease of all existence!
O Rāma, who resides in the abode of Vaikuṇṭha!
O Rāma, who dwells in the state of eternal bliss!
107. O Rāma, Rāma! Victory to King Rāma! 108. O Rāma, Rāma! Victory to Sītā-Rāma!
O refuge, remover of fear, auspiciousness, Rāma of Daśaratha!
Victory, victory, auspicious Sītārāma!
Victory to Rāma, the bringer of auspiciousness! O Rāma, from whom arises the attainment of all auspicious prosperity!
O Rāma, showerer of the nectar of bliss! O you who are affectionate toward those who take refuge in you! Victory, victory, O Rāma!
Lord of the Raghus, Rāghava, King Rāma;
Sītārāma, the purifier of the fallen.
Praise be to You, O source of Kanaka, Ambara, Kamalāsana, and Janaka; the abode of all splendors; the sinless ground that serves as the dwelling for the minds of sages such as Sanaka and others.
O Rāma, son of Daśaratha, who crosses the surface of the earth, you are the long-desired object of desire for the leaders of the gods who have come for refuge.
O Rāma, who brings joy to the world by slaying the wives of the flesh-eaters;
O Rāma, whose deeds are marvelous in protecting the sacrifice of the son of Kuśika!
O Rāma, who liberated the wife of the householder Dhani-Gautama from her sin;
O Rāma, whose feet purify and are held in high esteem by the circle of sages!
O Rāma, who shattered the delicate bow of the Destroyer of Smara;
O Rāma, Lord of Sītā, who delights both gods and men.
O Rāma, whose body is as beautiful as the god armed with flowers (Kāmadeva), whose face is like a lotus;
O Rāma, who crushes the pride of those honored for their wealth and born of the Bhṛgu lineage!
O Rāma, ocean of the essence of compassion, affectionate toward those who bow before you,
O Rāma, the destroyer of worldly existence, your feet are my refuge.
I bow again and again to Śrī Rāma, the remover of calamities, the bestower of all prosperity,
and the delight of the world.
Salutations to Rāma, to Rāmacandra, to Rāmabhadra, to the Creator,
to the Lord of the Raghus, to the Protector, and to the husband of Sītā.
Salutation to the illustrious Hanumān: the abode of incomparable strength, whose body resembles a mountain of gold, the fire that consumes the forest of demons, and the foremost among the wise.
I bow to the son of the Wind, the treasury of all virtues, the sovereign of the monkeys, and the excellent messenger of the Lord of the Raghus. || 1 ||

I salute the Son of the Wind, that great jewel in the necklace of the Rāmāyaṇa, who turned the ocean into a mere puddle for a cow’s hoofprint and reduced the Rākṣasa to the size of a mosquito. || 2 ||
I pay homage to the heroic lord of monkeys, the delighter of Añjanā, the destroyer of Jānakī’s grief, the slayer of Akṣa, and the one who struck fear into Laṅkā. 3.
I bow with palms joined in reverence to that son of Añjanā, who sportingly leaped across the waters of the ocean and, taking up the fire of grief from the daughter of Janaka, burned Laṅkā with it.

I bow my head to the son of the Wind, the chief of the monkey hosts, the messenger of Śrī Rāma, who is as swift as thought, whose speed is equal to the wind, who has conquered his senses, and who is the most excellent among the wise. 5.
I meditate upon the son of the Wind-god, whose face is as crimson as collyrium, whose body is as lovely as the mountain of gold, and who dwells at the foot of the Pārijāta tree. 6.
Wherever there is the chanting of the glories of Raghunātha, there bow down to Māruti, the destroyer of the Rākṣasas, who stands with palms joined in reverence and eyes filled with tears. 7.
Thus ends the *Rāmāyaṇa* consisting of one hundred and eight names.
